paper.title: SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation
paper.citation: Biao Zhang, Mathias Müller, and Rico Sennrich. SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation. In The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2023.

sources.role: Target and protocol source. The assignment pointed at the OpenReview PDF, but openreview.net served an HTTP 403 bot challenge to both the fetch tool and curl on 2026-09-13, so the arXiv v1 copy of the same ICLR 2023 camera-ready was hashed instead. The arXiv copy carries the 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023' header and the same tables; the OpenReview record remains the canonical citation.

The authors' official implementation, linked from the paper abstract. Contains the SLTUNET model, the adapted SMKD sign-embedding pretraining code under smkd/, the evaluation metrics under eval/, the PHOENIX walk-through under example/, and the DGS3-T construction scripts under dgs3-t/. Master branch, latest commit dated 2023-07-10.

Authors' released trained models. phoenix.tar.gz was downloaded and verified on 2026-09-13 (1,014,073,705 bytes, gzip integrity OK, sha256 b0e708b7abe5689475905ad11ac578abb02eb0f9bf00b207bbd6d4342afe5152). It contains more than weights: signemb_ckpt/average.pt (519 MB) is the pretrained SMKD sign-embedding model, sltunet_ckpt/average-0.* (589 MB) is the checkpoint-averaged trained SLTUNET model, and it also ships the exact runtime configuration (sltunet_ckpt/param.json, infer.sh, signemb.sh, sltunet.sh, baseline.yaml, configs/phoenix14.yaml), the joint vocabulary (vocab.zero.drop), the BPE model (ende.bpe), and the MT test data (test.bpe.en/de). The csldaily, csldaily2, and dgs3-t archives are reachable but have not been downloaded. Note the range request was ignored by the server, so the whole 1 GB archive was fetched rather than a header slice.
sources.config_corroboration: sltunet_ckpt/param.json independently confirms the target configuration read from the paper: hidden_size 256, embed_size 256, num_heads 4, filter_size 4096, num_encoder_layer 6, num_decoder_layer 6, beam_size 8, decode_alpha 1.0, remove_bpe true, img_feature_size 1024, max_img_len 512. This matches system 15 of Table 2 (d=256, h=4, dff=4096, N^P_enc=1 + N^S_enc=5 = 6 encoder layers, N_dec=6) and Appendix A.1 (beam size 8).

sources.role: Upstream SMKD/VAC_CSLR implementation cited by the paper (footnote 1) as the sign embedding extractor. The sltunet repository vendors an adapted copy under smkd/, so the vendored copy pinned through published-code is the artifact that will actually run; this upstream is recorded because the paper cites it and because the paper reports retraining SMKD with a 2D ResNet34 backbone.

datasets.cloud_processing_basis: Already present in the study's approved shared 'datasets' Volume on Modal, which is the project's controlled store for approved data. This attempt mounts it read-only and adds nothing.
datasets.precomputed_features_note: The volume also holds features/phoenix14t.pami0.{train,dev,test}, which are the Camgoz et al. (2020b) sign embeddings. These are NOT the embeddings behind the target numbers: Table 2 row 1.1 shows that using Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings scores 21.21 B@4 on dev, whereas the SLTUNET result requires the authors' retrained SMKD embeddings with a 2D ResNet34 backbone (18.90 WER, row 15, 27.87 B@4). Reproducing the targets therefore requires SMKD pretraining from the videos in videos/, not reuse of these features. Using them instead would be a behaviour-changing protocol deviation and would reproduce a different table row.

datasets.name: MuST-C English-German
datasets.version_or_subset: v1.0, text side only (used as the MT auxiliary task for PHOENIX-2014T and DGS3-T)
datasets.license_or_permission: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per the MuST-C release; non-commercial research use. To be confirmed at the data gate.
datasets.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-13: no MuST-C directory exists in the shared 'datasets' Volume. The volume listing contains no must-c slug of any spelling. MuST-C is required as the MT auxiliary task in Equation 4 for every target, so it must be acquired under its own terms (registration at FBK, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) before any training run. Only the text side is needed, not the audio.
datasets.acquisition_note: Checked 2026-09-13. The official distribution channel is gone: mustc.fbk.eu returns NXDOMAIN, and ict.fbk.eu/must-c (the URL cited by the published repository's example/README.md) now 301-redirects to a generic FBK research-centres page. MuST-C is no longer listed on the FBK MT unit resources page at mt.fbk.eu/resources/. Third-party Hugging Face re-uploads exist for German but carry contradictory licence metadata (afl-3.0 and apache-2.0 on a corpus released as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and are CSV conversions rather than the original release, so their identity and licence basis cannot be established without a reference copy to compare against. Archive check 2026-09-13: the last live snapshot of the FBK page (2023-05-28) already showed the download section as '(available soon...)', so the corpus had no working public download even while the page was up. The only external links on that page were two Google Drive README documents for v3.0 and v2.0, both now HTTP 404. No direct data URL was ever archived.
datasets.release_history: MuST-C release history, recovered 2026-09-13 from the Internet Archive snapshot of https://ict.fbk.eu/must-c/ dated 2023-05-28 (the last snapshot returning HTTP 200): v1.0 covers 8 directions, English into Dutch, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish; v1.1 is an IWSLT-2019 special release adding English-Czech, text only; v1.2 covers 14 directions and is the first release containing Chinese; v2.0 covers English into German, Chinese, and Japanese; v3.0 covers English-German only.
datasets.needed_for: Training only. The MT task is part of the Equation 4 training objective; inference from a trained checkpoint does not require MuST-C, as the authors' infer.sh confirms.
datasets.identity_fingerprint: Di Gangi et al. (2019) Table 2 gives the En-De section as 2,093 talks and 234K sentences. The paper under reproduction reports 229K En-De training samples, consistent with v1.0 minus the held-out dev (1.4K) and test (2.5K) segments described in section 3.4. Any candidate copy should be checked against these counts before use.

experiments.system: SLTUNET, final configuration (system 15 of Table 2): d=256, h=4, dff=4096, N^P_enc=1, N^S_enc=5, N_dec=6, CTC alpha=0.3, stochastic BPE dropout (rate 0.2, stochastic rate 0.6), Xavier gain 0.5, sign-frame random crop and horizontal flip, trained on the Equation 4 multi-task objective with MT data, using sign embeddings from the retrained SMKD model with a 2D ResNet34 backbone. Evaluated end-to-end (Sign2Text).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Average of the best 10 checkpoints ranked by dev-set Sign2Text performance, then beam search with beam size 8 and a length penalty tuned on the dev set (paper Appendix A.1; repository checkpoint_averaging.py and example/test.sh).

gates.reason: Materially changed by the released artifacts. The dominant cost was expected to be SMKD pretraining from video, but the authors' phoenix.tar.gz ships signemb_ckpt/average.pt, the pretrained SMKD sign-embedding model itself, alongside the checkpoint-averaged trained SLTUNET model. Three paths now exist and they answer different questions: (1) inference only from the released SLTUNET checkpoint, which verifies the authors' artifact and the evaluation pipeline but reproduces no training; (2) SLTUNET training from the released SMKD embeddings, which reproduces the paper's own training but inherits their sign encoder and still needs MuST-C; (3) full reproduction including SMKD pretraining from video, which is the only path that reproduces the whole pipeline. None has been costed, because no environment exists yet.
gates.required_action: Decide which of the three paths the study wants, then cost it from a representative preflight and apply the compute gate. Path 1 is cheap and unblocked by MuST-C and is the recommended first step regardless, because it validates the container, decoding, and metric implementation against published numbers before anything expensive runs. Paths 2 and 3 both require resolving MuST-C first. Whichever is chosen, the reused artifacts must be recorded as such: a score obtained from the authors' own weights is artifact verification, not a reproduction of their training, and cannot close a target as if it were.
evidence: Paper section 5.1: the SMKD model is pretrained on each benchmark separately on the Sign2Gloss task.
Paper section 5.2: replacing Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings with the retrained SMKD model gives +1.41 BLEU, and the ResNet34 backbone change a further +0.31 BLEU.

The released infer.sh wires these together directly: smkd_model_path=signemb_ckpt/average.pt with the SLTUNET checkpoint in output_dir=sltunet_ckpt, decoding eval_task='sign2text'.

gates.reason: The MuST-C release supplying the En-Zh MT data for the CSL-Daily experiments is not identified, and the primary sources now rule out the cited one. Di Gangi et al. (2019) state MuST-C covers English into 8 languages and list them; Chinese is not among them. The FBK release history confirms Chinese first appears in v1.2. The paper under reproduction cites Di Gangi et al. (2019) for 185K En-Zh samples, and the published repository pins v1.0 for En-De only. The En-Zh data therefore came from v1.2 or v2.0, and nothing states which.
gates.required_action: Determine whether the v1.2 or the v2.0 English-Chinese training portion contains about 185K segments and use that to identify the release. If the counts do not discriminate, this becomes an author-contact question, which is gated until after an independent attempt. Until resolved, any CSL-Daily training run using a guessed release is conditional evidence, not a produced target. This gate does not block the PHOENIX-2014T targets.
evidence: Paper section 5.1: 'We employ MuST-C English-German (En-De, 229K samples) and English-Chinese (En-Zh, 185K samples) (Di Gangi et al., 2019) as the augmented MT data for PHOENIX-2014T/DGS3-T and CSL-Daily, respectively.'
Published repository example/README.md step 1: 'Get MuST-C En-De dataset from FBK; note we used the data in v1.0' — v1.0 is pinned for En-De only.
Di Gangi et al. (2019) describes MuST-C as covering English into eight languages: Dutch, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish. Chinese is not among them.
The En-De figure of 229K is consistent with v1.0; the En-Zh figure of 185K must therefore come from a different release.

Di Gangi et al. (2019), abstract and section 1: MuST-C covers 'English into 8 languages' — German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian. Table 2 lists exactly these 8 sections.

MuST-C release history, recovered 2026-09-13 from the Internet Archive snapshot of https://ict.fbk.eu/must-c/ dated 2023-05-28 (the last snapshot returning HTTP 200): v1.0 covers 8 directions, English into Dutch, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish; v1.1 is an IWSLT-2019 special release adding English-Czech, text only; v1.2 covers 14 directions and is the first release containing Chinese; v2.0 covers English into German, Chinese, and Japanese; v3.0 covers English-German only.

environment_plan.published_requirements: python==3.8, tensorflow==1.15 (repository README 'Requirement'); no requirements.txt or lockfile is published.
environment_plan.base_image_conflict: The repository's standard GPU base image ghcr.io/sign-language-processing/reproduction:latest supplies NVIDIA NGC PyTorch. SLTUNET is TensorFlow 1.15, which needs CUDA 10.0 / cuDNN 7.x and will not run on that image, so a paper-specific Dockerfile is expected. This is an environment adaptation, not a change to the published code, and the exact image has not been chosen or built yet.
environment_plan.video_decoding: The published SLTUNET training path consumes precomputed SMKD sign features in .h5 files rather than decoding video, so no video decoder is introduced for it. The upstream SMKD feature-extraction step does read frames and is where simple-video-utils would apply if that step is rerun.
environment_plan.planned_first_check: Evaluation-path preflight using the authors' released PHOENIX artifacts: run the shipped infer.sh against the PHOENIX videos already in the shared Volume, using signemb_ckpt/average.pt and the checkpoint-averaged SLTUNET model, then score with eval/metrics.py against the Table 4 end-to-end test numbers. This needs no MuST-C and no SMKD pretraining, so it is unblocked by the open data gates, and it validates the TensorFlow 1.15 container, the decoding settings, and the metric implementation before any expensive run. Its result is artifact verification, not a reproduction of the authors' training.

open_questions: Whether the study wants the DGS3-T targets pursued at all, given that permission from the University of Hamburg is a prerequisite and may not be obtainable within the study.

Whether reproducing Table 4/5 requires retraining SMKD sign embeddings from video (the expensive path the paper describes) or whether the authors' released checkpoints and any released features make a shorter path defensible; this changes the compute estimate by a large factor and has not been costed.
